To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
salivaricin is a potent inhibitor of cell wall biosynthesis and is not a pore-forming antibiotic.
the lantibiotics nisin A and salivaricin A have different bactericidal modes of action.
salivaricin-B is an effective bacteriocin that interferes with cell wall biosynthetic processes and does not induce cell membrane permeabilisation or dissipation of the membrane potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mode of action and the mechanism of action of the type AII peptide antibiotic salivaricin.
the mode of action, structure-activity relationship and mechanism of resistance development of salivaricins.
the mode of action and the potential for the application of the lantipeptide salivaricin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
salivaricin is a bactericidal lantibiotic that kills susceptible bacteria via interference with peptidogycan synthesis, but without causing cell lysis.
salivaricin is a lantibiotic which acts by interfering with cell wall biosynthetic enzymes.
salivaricin acts on susceptible bacteria by interfering with cell wall biosynthetic processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
salivaricin is a bactericidal lantibiotic with a mode of action that is distinct from other members of the lantipeptide family.
salivaricin-B is a lantibiotic with a unique mode of action.
salivaricin acts by interfering with the final step of peptidoglycerol synthesis in the cell wall biosynthesis pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
salivaricin is a novel type of lantibiotics which does not act by membrane disruption, but rather by interference with cell wall biosynthetic enzymes.
salivaricin is a potent bactericidal lantibiotic that kills bacteria through an alternative mode of action to nisin A.
salivaricin is a lantibiotic which does not act on the cytoplasmic membranes of susceptible bacteria, but rather on the biosynthesis of cell walls.
